To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Transformer architecture can be successfully used to correct the output of a phrase-based MT system; 2) a sequence-level loss function is crucial to avoid exposure bias and improve the quality of the corrections; 3) a multi-source model can be trained to correct neural outputs with gains that are statistically significant but not as high as in the case of a phrase-based system.
(1) the proposed multi-source neural model is effective for APE, (2) the Transformer is a promising architecture for the task, and (3) the proposed combined losses are beneficial for the training.
the Transformer architecture, combined with sequence-level loss functions, is a powerful framework for the APE task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a neural APE system based on the Transformer model and with the use of sequence-level loss functions.

the following contributions: (i) the first multi-source APE system based on Transformer; (ii) the first APE system that uses a sequence-level loss function; (iii) the first ABE system that uses a combined loss function.
the development of an APE model based both on Transformer and sequence-level loss functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed multi-source approach is able to consistently outperform the single-source baseline, both in terms of TER and BLEU, and that it is robust to the different quality of the initial outputs, as well as to the different training setups.
the Transformer model with combined losses is a very promising approach to the APE task.

the Transformer-based architecture and the multi-source approach, when combined with sequence-level loss functions and a careful tuning of the training parameters, can lead to a significant improvement in the quality of the postediting process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel neural multi-source model for APE that, despite the high quality of the initial MT outputs, still improves the final translation.
the proposed model can be successfully applied to the APE task, and that it can provide improvements over the state of the art in terms of both TER and BLEU scores.

we show that the combination of the Transformer model with the sequence-level loss function allows to achieve the best results in the task, even if the initial MT outputs are very poor, and that the Transformer model is able to correct NMT outputs with a higher quality than that of the PBSMT ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Transformer-based models can be successfully applied to the APE task, even though the quality of the initial MT output is low.
the proposed Transformer model is competitive with the best performing systems of the shared task.

the combination of the Transformer architecture and sequence-level loss functions allows to improve the quality of the APE system in both the considered subtasks, and that our approach can be successfully extended to other NLP tasks.
